questions.question: Which redirect path best protects latency and availability?
options: Redirect service -> analytics database -> mapping store -> destination
Redirect service -> cache -> mapping store on a miss, with click events emitted asynchronously
Redirect service -> code allocator -> primary database -> analytics stream
Redirect service -> synchronous abuse review -> mapping store -> destination
questions.explanation: The latency-sensitive path should perform only the work needed to resolve the destination. Cache misses may reach the mapping store, while analytics remains asynchronous and non-blocking.

questions.question: Peak redirect traffic is 350K requests per second and the cache hit rate is 90%. Approximately how many mapping-store reads must the design handle?
options: 3.5K reads per second
35K reads per second
315K reads per second
350K reads per second
questions.explanation: A 90% hit rate leaves 10% of requests as misses: 350K x 0.10 = 35K mapping-store reads per second. The store also needs protection for lower hit rates during cache failure.

questions.question: Which operation requires the strongest consistency boundary?
options: Aggregating click counts for a dashboard
Replicating a popular mapping to an edge cache
Reserving a custom alias so two users cannot own the same code
Sampling redirect events for long-term analytics
questions.explanation: Code ownership is a uniqueness invariant. Creation and custom-alias reservation must prevent two active mappings from claiming the same short code.

questions.question: Why should an expired short code return 410 Gone without being immediately recycled?
options: It makes the code easier to cache forever.
It prevents stale caches and old messages from redirecting users to a new owner's destination.
It guarantees analytics are strongly consistent.
It removes the need to store an expiration timestamp.
questions.explanation: Immediate reuse can combine stale infrastructure state with a new mapping and send users to the wrong destination. A tombstone or reuse delay preserves safer semantics.

questions.question: What is the safest response to a distributed-cache outage?
options: Send every miss directly to the mapping store without limits.
Fail every redirect until the cache is fully restored.
Use bounded fallback, request coalescing, admission control, and protection for the mapping store.
Move click analytics into the redirect process to reduce dependencies.
questions.explanation: An unbounded fallback can turn a cache outage into a storage outage. Coalescing, rate limits, stale serving where allowed, and storage protection contain the failure.

questions.question: Which partitioning approach best supports URL-shortener growth?
options: Partition by the first character and never rebalance.
Hash stable short codes into ownership ranges and move ranges gradually as capacity changes.
Partition by creation timestamp so all new writes share one partition.
Store every mapping on one global primary because redirects are read-heavy.
questions.explanation: Hashing stable lookup keys spreads traffic, while movable ownership ranges support gradual rebalancing without coupling partition placement to one machine forever.
